subject: physics
question_text: Where in its path is the velocity of a particle in simple harmonic motion maximum, and where is its acceleration maximum? Write both maximum values.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The velocity
lines: v = ω√(A² − y²), which is largest when y = 0.
So the velocity is maximum at the MEAN
position, where the acceleration is zero:
steps.why: The particle has been pulled inward all the way from the extreme, so the mean position is where it has picked up the most speed.
common_mistakes: Saying the velocity is maximum at the extreme positions, where it is actually zero.

recall.must_convey: That v is maximum at the mean position and equals A omega.
reject: a max is omega squared A

steps.memory_tip: Put y = 0 into v = ω√(A² − y²): the square root gives A, so v_max = Aω.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The mean position and v_max = Aω are both needed for it.

steps.label: The acceleration
lines: a = −ω²y, which is largest when y = ±A.
So the acceleration is maximum at the EXTREME
positions, where the velocity is zero:
steps.why: The two maxima sit at opposite ends of the path: where the particle moves fastest it is not accelerating, and where it stops it is pulled hardest.
common_mistakes: Placing both maxima at the same point.
Writing a_max = −ω²A as the value — the maximum is the magnitude ω²A; the minus sign only records the direction, toward the mean position (at y = +A the acceleration is −ω²A).

recall.must_convey: That a is maximum at the extreme positions and equals omega squared A.
accept: a max is omega squared A

steps.memory_tip: a_max = ω v_max = ω²A. Each step from y to v to a brings in one more ω.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The extreme positions and a_max = ω²A. Give the magnitude, not the sign.

insider_note: Each mark needs a place and a value, so write v_max = Aω and a_max = ω²A as well as the mean and extreme positions.
